text:
You fleet approaches the wreckage of a vast Domain Armada military logistics hub. Such facilities were capable of servicing entire naval flotillas, and once formed the locus of Domain efforts to stabilize and maintain control of key frontier sectors. However, they are typically located in the core worlds of each sector, and your databanks have no records of this particular station that straddles the edge of the hyperspace abyss.

A cursory scan indicates the superstructure has sustained heavy damage, but not of a type that is normally seen in combat. Beneath a tangled mass of empty ship gantries, the station's surface is covered in unusual hull breaches that more resemble mandible bite marks than typical anti-ship weapon impacts. 

Sending forth salvage teams to explore the interior may shed light on what happened here, but something about this place stirs a deep sense of dread within you. Whatever its secrets, you feel it in your bones that it should not be disturbed.

text:
You fleet returns to the location of the abandoned military outpost. A twisted mass of wreckage barely held together by its own gravity outlines the skeleton of a once mighty fortress. Sifting through the debris, you find tantalizing clues pointing to the presence of the 6th Domain Battlegroup, predecessors of the 14th who went on to form the Hegemony. But did they create this threat, or were they trying to put an end to it? The wreckage stubbornly refuse to yield an answer.

Following your first engagement with the Infected ships, your salvage teams uncovered a set of old Domain-era signal protocols that were still embedded in the compromised systems. Broadcasting the signal in deep hyperspace may be enough to lure another fleet to your location, although there is no telling just how many drones will show up at a time.

As for these ruins, there is nothing more left for you here.

text:
"I don't like the look of these broken ship gantries," says the ops chief, pointing at a holographic display of the station. "Seems like there was quite the fleet docked here once upon a time, and they all tried to get away in a hurry, with zero regard for safe undocking procedures. That's what I'd call a clue. As for the station itself, scans are showing the whole structure was hollowed out by... something. There's an intact section, here. But if whatever caused this mess is still inside that pocket, I'm not sure it's a good idea to open it up."

A vast internal docking bay is highlighted on the station hologram, uniquely undisturbed and tantalizingly close. You could make a grab for it yourself, but such a find may also be of great interest to Tri-Tachyon Special Acquisitions on Eochu Bres, assuming you can gain access to their director.

The normally unflappable ops chief turns to you with a look of concern. "It's your call, captain. Shall we go in for a look?"

The salvage teams are grateful for your decision, and if they are disappointed in their meager finds, they hide it well. Several weapons of unknown provenance are found among the wreckage, the most notable of which being embedded inside the almost fully intact forward section of a heavily modified Onslaught-class battleship. The built-in energy weapons are extracted with great care, and now await installation on a compatible battleship.

Whatever other secrets the station may have held are well and truly lost. But you remain alive, and so does your crew.

text:
Your ops chief begins to monitor several displays at once as the teams make their way inside the hangar. A wealth of scanned data is passed to your flagship. Soon an enterprising salvor even manages to activate an old backup generator and turn on the lights. There, on a grainy camera feed, you spot the unmistakable outline of a Legion-class battlecarrier. 

But something is wrong with the ship. The hull is twisted and strange, covered in a thick layer of machinery resembling cancerous growths. And then the growths begin to move.
options: asmStationInteractSalvage1:Continue

text:
"Get out of there!" Your ops chief barks. "Drop everything and get back to the shuttle, right now!"

Even as the order is obeyed, every camera feed is blinded by a brilliant flash. An arc of voltaic lightning tears through the hangar, causing a cloud of smaller automatons to leap off the Legion and towards the glowing gash in the hull. They feast upon rivulets of molten metal, while their bodies begin to twist and grow.

The footage is cut short as the salvors make a hasty escape, their shuttle returning in record time. While your fleet moves to a safer distance, you watch the station tear itself apart like an overripe melon, spilling forth a throng of murderous machines.

"That is an annoyingly vague question," she says, although her tone does not sound more annoyed than usual.

"To summarize, you uncovered early Expansion-Era Domain Armada warships that have been retrofitted with Explorarium automation suites, along with additional changes that have altered the hulls to be ideal breeding grounds for Threat fragments. The latter revisions are crude, but interesting."

text:
Glamor-Rotanev's eyes blink rapidly again. She does not appear to be looking at you.

"The Threat are devourers, not infectants. They do not hijack a host body during standard operations, but rather seek to break it down for raw materials to use in their self replication process. The parasitism you witnessed requires extensive and deliberate engineering efforts to achieve. Furthermore, while the Threat have exhibited a limited capacity for incorporating foreign technology, what passes for design patters among their kind bear no resemblance to the retrofitting present on these so called infected ships."

Her lips form a thin smile. She has given you the information. It is your responsibility to make sense of it.

text:

She pauses for just a moment.

"And before you ask. No, I have no idea for what purpose."

id: # Handing in the PK - Persean League

options: pk_turnInPL:"Would the league be in need of a planetkiller?"
notes: #Bringing up this topic will make TT Arroyo unhappy

text:
$PersonRank $personLastName stares at you in alarm.

"Don't tell me you're harboring a live planetkiller in orbit."
options: pk_turnInPL2:"Don't worry. It's encrypted and inert. So do you want it or not?"

text: "I see," $heOrShe nods and thinks for a moment. "The League would happily dispose of such a dangerous device for you. I am authorized to release a suitable finder's fee of 500,000 credits in exchange for it, or..."
options: pk_turnInPL3:"Or?"

text:
$personLastName takes a moment to compose $himOrHerself.

"I'm in the middle of a rather delicate situation with the Navarchs," $heOrShe says. "Around five cycles ago, the League and the Diktat signed a major arms deal that saw us come into possessing of several new fleet carriers. The originals were... we'll, I won't mince words. They were atrocious parade fodder. But after our forge engineers had a chance to clear out the blueprint of all its Diktat cruft, we ended up with a fine ship."
options:
pk_turnInPL4:"I don't see how that's a problem."
pk_turnInPLrude:"Stop talking. I'm not interested."

text:
"There's no need for that," $heOrShe frowns. "I'll be going now. We can talk again once you've had a chance to learn some manners."

The line is unceremoniously cut.
options: cutCommLink:Attend to other business

text:
"The problem is the Navarchs don't want to have anything to do with it. Buying carriers from the Sindrians while we were fully capable of adapting our own design from a Domain template was never a good look, and many of the Navarchs feel the ship is cursed, or beneath them, or both. That's where you come in."

$HeOrShe brings up the schematics for the Proteus-class carrier, and to $hisOrHer credit, the design looks like a capable enough warship that combines heavy missile firepower with a decent complement of strike craft for long range engagements.
options: pk_turnInPL5:Continue

text:
"So here's what I propose. In exchange for the planetkiller, I will transfer a fully armed Porteus command carrier to your fleet. We'll keep quiet on the part of how you got it, avoid spooking any of our neighbors. And if you happen to put the ship to good use, the Fikenhild press will start putting out puff pieces on your exploits. Hopefully that'll be enough to shame the Navarchy into finally doing their jobs."

$PersonRank $personLastName pauses for a moment to let you think it over. "What do you say, captain? I'll help you dispose of a rad hot piece of technology you really shouldn't have in your possession, and you'll help me give the Proteus a much needed PR boost. It's a win-win."
options:
pk_turnInPLmoney:"I'll take the credits if it's all the same to you."
pk_turnInPLship:"Sure, let's see what this ship can do."
pk_turnInPLnm:"I'm going to need time to think this over."

text:
"Israfil, the Four Winged Glory, the Herald of the End."

Rabasi Kato closes her eyes and takes a deep breath. Your psych profiling software shows she is in a state of extreme stress, but the indicators of delusional thinking and religious mania are surprisingly low, despite her odd choice of words.

"Let me explain. Several cycles ago, I was contacted by an AI godmind. The being called itself Israfil, although it goes by many names. It showed me prophecies of the Sector's future, except these were not religious visions but interstellar data extrapolations of cause and effect more sophisticated than anything I've ever seen before. Then, one by one, the damned predictions came to pass, and they all led to one thing..."
options:
mission_project_mayfly_parley4:"Let me guess, the Third AI War."
mission_project_mayfly_battle:"I've heard enough. Time to put you down, mad dog."
